scripts/GATES.md:
| `scripts/check-layering.sh` | contracts are siblings in the import hierarchy: no cross-contract import, no shared module importing a contract, and the `Blanc/Composition/*` stratum strictly downstream of both. Each `COMPOSITION` entry explicitly declares a nonempty tuple of distinct `CONTRACTS` keys; a composition may import only those contract families and compositions whose declared families are a subset of its own. Unknown families, malformed declarations and missing classification entries fail closed. `python3 -B scripts/check-layering-controls.py --composition-only` exercises this production classifier and import relation on a minimal temporary source tree, including positive, undeclared-family, superset and schema controls, without Lean or a green corpus; the full control command still includes the existing Lean-header, architecture and discovery controls. Its header-only reader follows Lean 4.32.1's `public? meta? import all? identWithPartialTrailingDot` grammar, including quoted and Lean `isLetterLike` identifier components, nested/trailing comments and line-spanning whitespace; it stops at the first non-header command. It fails closed on unterminated header comments/strings, incomplete trailing-dot names, `public import all`, and reversed `meta public import` modifiers, each paired with Lean. `imports_of` is category-agnostic: it reads a future local module without consulting the classification table, so later category rules reuse the reader. A fifth check attaches a discovery obligation to the same SHARED classification: every active `scripts/proof-recipes.toml` recipe whose `owner_module` is classified shared must have that module path cited in `docs/COMMON_API.md`, and every `Blanc/*.lean` path that file cites must exist — the missing-entry and stale-entry directions of a reusable facility the need-first registry cannot reach. Both populations are asserted non-empty, so a registry reworded out of the check's sight fails rather than passing over nothing; it judges reachability only and is deliberately not a similarity detector. A sixth check closes the population the fifth cannot see: check 5 binds only a shared module that *owns an active recipe*, so a SHARED module with no recipe escaped it entirely — the since-archived SymbolicProgram module shipped as a 1,091-line shared facility with no `docs/COMMON_API.md` entry and no recipe while the gate reported green. Check 6 therefore attaches the discovery obligation to the SHARED classification itself: every module the table calls shared must have its path cited in `docs/COMMON_API.md`, and the only escape is a `DISCOVERY_EXEMPT` row naming the module and the concrete reason it is not a facility an author could be told to find (a compatibility re-export that declares nothing, the registry's own machinery, a control fixture). That table is validated in both directions — an exemption for a module that is absent, no longer shared, or now cited fails — so it prunes itself instead of absorbing the next shipped facility. Check 6 requires no recipe (`docs/COMMON_API.md`'s own workflow makes a recipe conditional on a reliable goal shape existing), judges no entry's quality, and binds exactly the SHARED-registration-to-registry-entry relation: an edit to an already-cited shared file is unaffected. Since 2026-11-01 a citation counts for check 6 (and for check 5's missing-entry direction) only inside the need-first tree — the Root section or a `## E — …` through `## C — …` need section, outside fenced code — so one citation appended below every branch, in the closing workflow, or fenced as code no longer satisfies it; the stale-entry direction still reads every citation. A seventh check (2026-11-01) holds the generated shared-module inventory `docs/MODULE_INVENTORY.md` byte-identical to `scripts/generate-module-inventory.py`'s rendering of the SHARED table, each shared module's own header summary and the registry branches citing it, so a hand edit or a stale inventory fails here (regenerate with `--write`). Check 11 (2026-11-08, whitelist W4): the shared documents `README.md`, `PORTING.md`, `docs/COMMON_API.md` and `scripts/GATES.md` name no contract or composition module of any family, live or released (from its release manifest), by path or dotted name, nor a directory all of whose modules are one family's; a family's uses of the shared API live in `docs/claim-map/<key>.md`, and the lines that could not move without rewording are listed in `DOC_LAYERING_ALLOWED` (each must still match; its size is pinned). Checks 8-10 (2026-11-08, whitelist live corpus) read `scripts/live-set.toml`: `CONTRACTS` holds exactly the live keys and no released key appears in `CONTRACTS` or as a `COMPOSITION` family; a module on disk that a release manifest lists and nothing live classifies fails as belonging to that released key, so a released family cannot come back without a restore; and `Blanc.lean` is byte-identical to `scripts/generate-root.py`'s rendering (every classified module, sorted, minus the two proof-recipe modules `scripts/AxiomCheck.lean` imports itself). `scripts/check-layering-controls.py` independently pairs each accepted form with Lean elaboration (rule and rationale in `README.md`) | 8 contracts, 805 modules, 2016 non-root checked, 152 compositions; 40 shared-facility recipes; 621/623 shared modules cited, 2 exemptions; 11 accepted-form, 3 rejected-header, 3 non-import, 3 malformed-header, 3 architecture, 5 composition-edge, 4 discovery, 5 shared-coverage, 2 inventory, 4 live-set and 1 category-agnostic controls | sub-second (latest at the retained library; ledger median 0.24 s of 12 record(s), which may include pre-retirement runs, imported 2026-11-06) |
